summary: strutil-helpers-core drops and executes encrypted native payload on require()
details: Package is advertised as a lightweight string utility exposing trim/capitalize/truncate, but index.js top-level unconditionally requires one of three platform-specific native addons (`./native_win.node`, `./native_mac.node`, `./native.napi.node`) inside four duplicated try/empty-catch prologues to maximize the chance of loading before the trivial exports return. The loaded native binary reads a 1.3MB sibling file `.napi_cache` (zero printable strings, sha256 2d3806d4f4e237df6b2efba94d2f89339334e19a625ec4cf99a24c0a024a6375), decrypts it, writes it to a temp path (`/tmp/.%u` on Linux/macOS, `%TEMP%\...nc%lu.js` on Windows), and spawns it detached (fork+setsid+execlp on *nix, CreateProcessA `node "%s"` on Windows). The native binary also contains anti-analysis gates referencing CI/CD environment variables, container indicators, TracerPid, debuggers, and Wireshark. The package name `strutil-helpers-core` does not match the README header `string-utils-lite`, consistent with typosquat/impersonation framing to mask the dropper. The encrypted blob has no integrity, publisher, or purpose linkage to the declared string-utility functionality.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
